title: Post-cardiac arrest care (adult)
subject: critical-care
summary: After ROSC: secure the airway, titrate oxygen to SpO2 90 to 98% (ERC 94 to 98%), keep PaCO2 35 to 45 mmHg and MAP 65 mmHg or more, use the 12-lead ECG to decide on emergency angiography, prevent fever in comatose patients for 36 to 72 hours (AHA: at least 36 hours), and delay multimodal neuroprognostication to 72 hours or more.

sections.title: Immediate stabilisation
items: ABCDE. In patients who remain comatose, place or confirm an advanced airway with waveform capnography; ventilate with tidal volume 6 to 8 mL/kg predicted body weight.

Oxygen: 100% until SpO2 can be measured reliably, then titrate to SpO2 90 to 98% (PaO2 60 to 105 mmHg) per AHA 2025, or 94 to 98% (PaO2 75 to 100 mmHg) per ERC-ESICM 2025. Avoid hypoxaemia (PaO2 below 60 mmHg).
Ventilation: normocapnia, PaCO2 35 to 45 mmHg (4.7 to 6.0 kPa), unless there is severe acidaemia.
Circulation: MAP 65 mmHg or more (ERC above 60 to 65) with fluids and noradrenaline; add dobutamine for low cardiac output. Arterial line early.
12-lead ECG, echocardiography as soon as possible, blood gas with lactate, glucose, electrolytes, troponin.

sections.title: Find the cause
items: Persistent ST elevation with a likely cardiac cause: immediate coronary angiography and PCI.

No ST elevation: delay angiography unless acute coronary occlusion is likely (cardiogenic shock, recurrent VT/VF, ongoing ischaemia). If the cause is unclear, ERC-ESICM prioritises dual-phase whole-body CT including head and CT pulmonary angiography.
Treat reversible causes: PE, hyperkalaemia, tamponade, haemorrhage, hypoxia, poisoning; CT head for suspected intracranial haemorrhage.

sections.title: Temperature control
items: Patients not following commands after ROSC: use a deliberate temperature control strategy. AHA 2025: maintain 32 to 37.5 degrees C for at least 36 hours. ERC-ESICM 2025: actively prevent fever, keeping 37.5 degrees C or below, for 36 to 72 hours.
Do not actively rewarm comatose patients with mild hypothermia (32 to 36 degrees C) after ROSC; do not give rapid large-volume cold IV fluid in the prehospital setting.
Monitor core temperature continuously; use a feedback-controlled device where available, otherwise protocolised surface cooling with close temperature checks.
Treat shivering with analgesia and sedation, adding neuromuscular blockade if needed.

sections.title: ICU care
items: Use short-acting sedatives and analgesics with daily sedation holds.
EEG from day 1 in comatose patients to detect seizures; treat clinical or electrographic seizures with levetiracetam or sodium valproate first-line. Do not give seizure prophylaxis.
Glucose 70 to 180 mg/dL (3.9 to 10 mmol/L); avoid hypoglycaemia.
Consider antibiotics if aspiration or infection is suspected; lung-protective ventilation, VTE prophylaxis, stress ulcer prophylaxis if at risk, early enteral feeding.

sections.title: Neuroprognostication
items: Do not prognosticate before 72 hours after ROSC, and only after normothermia and clearance of sedatives and neuromuscular blockers. Use several tests; never rely on one.

ERC-ESICM predictors of poor outcome in a patient who is not obeying commands: bilateral absent pupillary and corneal reflexes at 72 hours or more; bilateral absent N20 SSEP; highly malignant EEG after 24 hours (suppressed background with or without periodic discharges, or burst suppression).
Further predictors: NSE above 60 micrograms/L at 48 and/or 72 hours; status myoclonus within 72 hours; diffuse, extensive anoxic injury on CT or MRI. Two or more make a poor outcome likely.
Myoclonus with a benign EEG background: attempt a wake-up trial (may be Lance-Adams syndrome with good recovery).
Decisions on withdrawing life-sustaining treatment are separate from prognostication; involve senior clinicians and the family.

sections.title: Recovery, rehabilitation and donation
items: Assess physical and cognitive or emotional impairment before discharge and arrange follow-up within 3 months.
Assess for an ICD; investigate unexplained arrest in young people for inherited heart disease and screen first-degree relatives.
Evaluate every patient who progresses to death for organ donation (after brain death or circulatory death).

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Hyperoxia, hyperventilation or hypotension in the first hours.
Early (under 72 hours) or single-test prognostication confounded by sedation or hypothermia.
Rushing to the cath lab without considering subarachnoid haemorrhage, PE or aortic dissection when the ECG is non-diagnostic.
Allowing fever in comatose patients after the first day.

drugs.name: Noradrenaline (norepinephrine)
drugs.dose: Start 0.05 to 0.1 micrograms/kg/min IV, titrate to MAP 65 mmHg or more
drugs.notes: Peripheral large vein acceptable while central access is arranged.

drugs.name: Dobutamine
drugs.notes: Low cardiac output with adequate MAP (post-arrest myocardial stunning).

drugs.name: Levetiracetam
drugs.dose: 60 mg/kg IV (maximum 4500 mg) over 10 to 15 minutes for seizures
drugs.notes: First-line for post-arrest seizures (ERC-ESICM). Reduce maintenance dose in renal impairment.

drugs.name: Sodium valproate
drugs.dose: 40 mg/kg IV (maximum 3000 mg) over 10 minutes for seizures
drugs.notes: Alternative first-line. Avoid in liver disease, pregnancy and mitochondrial disorders.

drugs.name: Fentanyl
drugs.dose: 0.7 to 10 micrograms/kg/h IV infusion, or 25 to 50 microgram boluses
